- **Copper smelting and bronze** [`copper_bronze`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/copper_bronze.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Copper from Cyprus, Spain and Etruria, tin from Spain and beyond Gaul. Lost-wax statues, vessels, fittings and water valves are routine work. Local: bronze workshops of Capua; Etruscan bronze founders.
- **Bloomery iron (wrought iron, forging, carburising)** [`bloomery_iron`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/bloomery_iron.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Elba ore is smelted in bloomeries at Populonia; smiths forge blooms into tools and weapons. Iron is never melted and stays dearer than a modern person expects. Local: Populonia and Elba; Puteoli (iron working and trade).
- **Hardening and tempering steel** [`steel_heat_treatment`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/steel_heat_treatment.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Smiths quench and judge by eye and file; results vary from blade to blade. Deliberate tempering by colour and the role of carbon are unknown. Elsewhere: Noricum, steel of the Magdalensberg region; Spain, Celtiberian sword smiths.
- **Cementation (blister) steel and case hardening** [`cementation_steel`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cementation_steel.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept high. Good steel comes from good ore (Noricum, Spain), not from a process. Smiths harden edges in charcoal without knowing why. Packing bars in charcoal in sealed clay boxes is new. Elsewhere: kingdom of Noricum (allied, trading through Aquileia).
- **Blast furnace and cast iron** [`blast_furnace_cast_iron`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/blast_furnace_cast_iron.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Iron that runs liquid is unknown and would be called spoiled. Needs a tall shaft, continuous strong blast and refractory lining; water-driven bellows do not exist. Elsewhere: Han China, state ironworks casting iron tools.
- **Smelting iron with coke** [`coke_iron`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/coke_iron.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low. Needs the blast furnace first. Italy has charcoal and almost no coal.
- **Puddling and rolling (wrought iron from pig iron with coal)** [`puddling_wrought_iron`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/puddling_wrought_iron.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low Elsewhere: Han China, 'stir-frying' cast iron into wrought iron.

Needs crucibles and a furnace that hold steel-melting heat for hours; Roman crucibles are for bronze and silver. Elsewhere: South India and Sri Lanka, crucible steel.

- **Refractories (fireclay, crucibles, furnace linings)** [`refractories_fireclay`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/refractories_fireclay.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Bronze founders, glassworkers and potters make crucibles and kiln linings from tempered clay, good to bronze and glass heat. Clays for steel heat must be found by trial.
- **Brass and metallic zinc** [`zinc_brass`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/zinc_brass.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Brass (orichalcum) is made in Asia Minor by heating copper with calamine and is prized. Caesar's prefect Clovius strikes brass coins in 45 BC. Metallic zinc is unknown. Elsewhere: Asia Minor (Phrygia, Bithynia), cementation brass.
- **Cupellation, parting and assaying of silver and gold** [`cupellation_assaying`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cupellation_assaying.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Silver is cupelled from lead ore in the Spanish mines; gold is parted from silver with salt; the touchstone tests purity. Lead is the cheap by-product that fills Rome's pipes. Local: mint at the temple of Juno Moneta; Spanish silver mines near Carthago Nova.
- **Mercury and amalgamation of gold and silver** [`mercury_amalgam`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mercury_amalgam.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Cinnabar from Sisapo in Spain is the costly red pigment, and quicksilver is roasted from it. Gilders lay gold leaf, and quicksilver serves to gild bronze. Fumes are not feared. Elsewhere: Sisapo (Almaden), Spain.
- **Lead is a cumulative poison** [`lead_hazard`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lead_hazard.md) — K2, use wrong, make easy, accept low. Nicander's poem describes white-lead poisoning, yet lead is everywhere: pipes, pans, cosmetics. Cato has must boiled to syrup 'in a copper or lead vessel'. The syrup sweetens and preserves wine. Local: plumbarii (lead-pipe makers); Cato, De agri cultura 105 and 107; wine growers and merchants.
- **Soldering, brazing and tinning** [`soldering_tinning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/soldering_tinning.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Tin-lead solder joins lead pipes and bronze vessels; goldsmiths braze. Tinning copper cookware is uncommon here.
- **Pottery, kilns and fired brick** [`fired_brick_ceramics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/fired_brick_ceramics.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Roof tiles, amphorae and storage jars are fired by the million, and Arretium has just begun its red-gloss tableware. Walls are tufa, rubble concrete and sun-dried brick, not fired brick. Local: potteries of Arretium.
- **Porcelain** [`porcelain`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/porcelain.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept medium. No known kaolin source and no kiln reaching 1300 degrees. Fine tableware is silver, glass or red-gloss pottery. Elsewhere: Han China, high-fired glazed stoneware (true porcelain comes later).
- **Glassmaking and glassblowing** [`glassmaking`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/glassmaking.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Glass is a luxury: core-formed flasks and cast or slumped bowls, mostly eastern imports. Blowing is just being tried on the Syro-Palestinian coast. An iron tube is the missing tool. Local: imported Hellenistic cast bowls and mosaic glass; eastern traders at Puteoli. Elsewhere: Syro-Palestinian coast and Jerusalem, first blown glass; Alexandria, luxury cast and mosaic glass.
- **Colourless and optical glass (cristallo, lead crystal, plate)** [`clear_glass`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/clear_glass.md) — K3, use partial, make hard, accept high. Colourless glass decolourised with antimony exists as cast luxury bowls, thick and seedy. Clear, bubble-free glass fit for lenses needs better furnaces, purer sand and stirring. Elsewhere: eastern Mediterranean glasshouses.
- **Glass mirrors (tin amalgam and silvering)** [`glass_mirrors`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/glass_mirrors.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept high. Mirrors are polished bronze or silver and a profitable trade. Glass mirrors need thin blown glass first; tin, lead and mercury for the backing are available.
- **Hydraulic lime, Roman concrete and Portland cement** [`hydraulic_cement`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/hydraulic_cement.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Lime with volcanic ash from Puteoli (pozzolana) sets under water and is standard for vaults, foundations and harbour moles. Portland cement would add little except early strength. Local: Puteoli (pulvis Puteolanus); Theatre of Pompey (concrete vaults, 55 BC); Caesar's builders at the Forum Iulium.
- **Reinforced concrete** [`reinforced_concrete`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/reinforced_concrete.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Builders trust mass and the arch; concrete in tension is not a concept. Hand-forged iron bar by the ton is ruinously dear and rusts in lime-ash concrete.
- **Papermaking** [`paper`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/paper.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Writing is on papyrus from Egypt, wax tablets and some parchment. Linen rags, hemp rope, mortars and screens exist. Papyrus is adequate and its importers will not welcome a rival. Local: papyrus dealers and booksellers; Atticus' copying slaves. Elsewhere: Egypt, papyrus making in the Nile Delta; Han China, coarse hemp paper used for wrapping.
- **Preparing textile fibres (wool, flax, cotton, silk)** [`textile_fibres`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/textile_fibres.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Wool and linen are spun by hand and woven on upright looms, largely in the household. Cotton and silk arrive as rare cloth from the East. Elsewhere: India, cotton; Cos, wild silk; China, silk reaching Rome through Parthia.
- **Tanning leather** [`leather_tanning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/leather_tanning.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Vegetable tanning with oak bark and galls, alum tawing for fine skins. The army consumes huge quantities for tents, shields and boots; tanners work across the Tiber. Local: tanners in Transtiberim.
